title: QBR: Solara Tech - Health Check
next_steps: Alex to send updated dedicated capacity pricing and burst options (due 2027-01-05)
Marco to schedule a 1-hour perf benchmark with Solara test set (week of 2027-01-11)
Priya to share QBR deck and audit log export instructions
Customer to confirm timeline for Dedicated pilot decision (target by 2027-01-18)
action_items: Alex Chen - Send revised pricing and committed capacity proposal - due 2027-01-05
Marco Ruiz - Run dedicated perf benchmark and share results - due 2027-01-15
Priya Kapoor - Share security and SOC2 docs + audit log extraction steps - due 2026-12-31
Jenna Lee - Provide 2 sample traffic traces and 5 worst-case prompts - due 2027-01-07
summary: Quarterly health check focused on usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment. Customer is evaluating a Dedicated pilot to stabilize tail latency and control unit economics; they raised SLO concerns during marketing spikes and asked for a perf benchmark. Action items and follow-ups defined.
topics: Usage and cost trends (token growth, embedding volume)
Reliability and recent incidents (latency spikes, 12/05 incident)
Roadmap alignment and upcoming feature requests
transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy holidays by the way, we'll keep this to 45 minutes. I'm Alex, AE here, with Priya and Marco from Redwood. Agenda is QBR health check - usage, cost, reliability, roadmap, and next steps. Jenna, Marcus, Samira from Solara, you good?
[00:00:14] Jenna Lee: Yep all good, thanks Alex. Short agenda is perfect, we have about 45 minutes.
[00:00:22] Priya Kapoor: Quick note, we posted the QBR deck in the calendar invite, link's in the chat if anyone wants to open it.
[00:00:30] Marcus Graham: Got it, opening now.
[00:00:35] Alex Chen: Great. To kick off, usage - from our side we've seen steady token growth month over month, Jenna you were at ~18% MoM last quarter, with embedding volume up after the search feature launch. How's that matching your expectations?
[00:00:50] Jenna Lee: Yeah that's about right, the search rollout drove more embeddings. We're also doing more rerank flows which spiked tokens per session. There are a couple of places where costs surprised us, like the afternoon traffic bursts last month.
[00:01:03] Marco Ruiz: On the bursts - we noticed two long-tail latency spikes that correlated with big batch jobs from your indexing pipeline, that was on 2026-12-05 where the 95th and 99th percentiles jumped. We have logs, but wanted to confirm that was the same window you saw.
[00:01:20] Samira Patel: Yeah that's the one, our batch indexer accidentally ran during peak hours; we pushed a fix but wanted guidance on preventing those cost/latency surprises.
[00:01:30] Alex Chen: Understood. Options: rate-limiting, separate routing for indexing jobs, or moving heavy batch jobs to off-peak with our burst policy. For more deterministic latency, Dedicated pools are helpful because you get reserved GPU capacity.
[00:01:45] Marcus Graham: Cost math is the sticking point. We liked hosted for simplicity but the unit economics during spikes are painful. Any quick back-of-envelope on Dedicated break-even?
[00:01:58] Marco Ruiz: For your load profile we estimate dedicated becomes attractive once sustained baseline throughput exceeds ~60k tokens/sec (note: rough). I know that's fuzzy — we'll run a tailored calc. Dedicated also lets you pin a quantized model variant which saves per-token CPU/GPU.
[00:02:16] Jenna Lee: Would that affect quality? We're sensitive to hallucinations on the support-summaries flow.
[00:02:23] Marco Ruiz: Good question — model variant and quantization profiles can slightly change output in edge cases. We recommend a small eval set; we'll run a delta check and share metrics (perplexity/ROUGE/QA accuracy on your prompts).
[00:02:38] Priya Kapoor: We'll also show historical quality regressions tied to model updates in the QBR slide 6, just to make sure we can monitor after any change.
[00:02:47] Alex Chen: Back to reliability — Samira you probably saw our incident postmortem for 12/05?
[00:02:53] Samira Patel: I skimmed the postmortem but didn't get all the KV cache details. There was mention of prefix caching and a fallback that triggered; could you explain?
[00:03:04] Marco Ruiz: Sure — in short, we cache common prompt prefixes and warm KV caches for recurrent sessions. In that incident the cache eviction policy hit because of an unexpected surge of unique session prefixes from the indexer; fallback to cold-start increased end-to-end latency.
[00:03:20] Jenna Lee: So the eviction threshold can be tuned?
[00:03:23] Marco Ruiz: Yes, and with Dedicated we can allocate larger KV cache memory and control eviction policies more aggressively. Also, we can blacklist the indexer service from prefix caching by route, so it doesn't displace production user sessions.
[00:03:36] Marcus Graham: That sounds promising. Priya, what visibility do we get on tracing? Our infra team needs per-route tracing and token-level cost dashboards.
[00:03:46] Priya Kapoor: You get per-route dashboards in Redwood Console, plus trace IDs on every request. We can extend retention for audit logs as an add-on. I'll include steps to configure SAML SSO for your org in the follow-up.
[00:03:58] Samira Patel: Perfect — also KMS support? Our security team requires customer-managed keys.
[00:04:04] Alex Chen: Yes, we support KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption with BYOK options for enterprise tiers. We'll put the exact docs in the follow-up.
[00:04:15] Jenna Lee: On timeline, we're trying to decide by mid-Jan if we go Dedicated pilot. Main blockers are cost approval and a quick perf validation.
[00:04:25] Alex Chen: Sounds reasonable. Proposed plan: Redwood runs a 1-week dedicated pilot with reserved baseline capacity + burst for a small committed fee. We'll run the perf benchmark with your test set and share cost projections.
[00:04:36] Marcus Graham: What's the smallest pilot size?
[00:04:39] Marco Ruiz: We can do a 2-GPU baseline for the pilot to mimic your sustained throughput; we have a template pilot agreement. It captures SLOs and a rollback/fallback policy.
[00:04:50] Jenna Lee: If we sign for pilot, how quickly can you provision?
[00:04:53] Alex Chen: Typically 3-5 business days once contract and payment are in place. We can prioritize your pilot in the backlog.
[00:05:00] Samira Patel: Do we need network work for VPC peering?
[00:05:03] Marco Ruiz: For Dedicated hosted in our cloud, no peering required; for Private (VPC/on-prem) we do need peering and extra infra work. Pilot can be hosted and still meet your latency goals.
[00:05:12] Jenna Lee: Great. A few product asks from our side: 1) better quota alerts tied to expected spend, 2) a per-model rollback button in the console, and 3) easier extraction of audit logs for compliance.
[00:05:24] Priya Kapoor: Noted — those map to our roadmap items. We'll prioritize audit log export and quota alerts for the next sprint; rollback UI is a product ask we'll raise with PM.
[00:05:35] Marcus Graham: On the cost side, can you send an example savings calc if we pin model v2-3 quantized vs v2 baseline?
[00:05:43] Marco Ruiz: Yes — we'll run a delta on compute cost and token throughput, plus expected quality delta on your eval prompts. Expect that in the benchmark results.
[00:05:52] Alex Chen: Any compliance or procurement questions?
[00:05:55] Jenna Lee: Procurement asked for SOC2 and a BAA template; also they asked about data residency for EU customers.
[00:06:03] Priya Kapoor: We have SOC2 Type II docs and a standard BAA, and we have EU region hosting options to restrict residency. I'll attach those.
[00:06:11] Samira Patel: Thanks, that should help.
[00:06:14] Alex Chen: Alright let's go into a quick walk-through of the usage slide — slide 3 shows tokens by flow: chat, search, rerank, indexer. Jenna you had flagged rerank rising heavily.
[00:06:26] Jenna Lee: Yeah rerank is up 3x since August. It's fine, but it's pushing us into higher billing tiers for embeddings.
[00:06:33] Marco Ruiz: We can discuss batching strategies for rerank to reduce per-token overhead, and a small caching layer for static queries. That often drops cost by 15-30% for customers with similar patterns.
[00:06:44] Marcus Graham: Is that something our infra team needs to change, or can Redwood enable it server-side?
[00:06:49] Marco Ruiz: Mostly server-side config, but we'll ask for a small client-side change to aggregate requests in your rerank pipeline. We'll include a snippet in the follow-up.
[00:06:58] Priya Kapoor: I'm noting that for the action items.
[00:07:02] Alex Chen: Quick check — any ongoing incidents besides the one in December?
[00:07:06] Samira Patel: No active incidents. We had a brief anomaly in latency on 11/02 but it was resolved.
[00:07:11] Marco Ruiz: We correlated that to a model update at the time; we now have canary rollouts which should prevent wide regressions.
[00:07:19] Jenna Lee: Good to know.
[00:07:21] Alex Chen: Ok, roadmap alignment — you mentioned a new search ranking feature in Q1. How tightly coupled is that to model latency?
[00:07:30] Jenna Lee: Pretty tight. Real-time user flow requires p95 < 250ms for the ranking endpoint.
[00:07:36] Marco Ruiz: We can meet that with Dedicated and prefix warmers; we'll show simulated latencies in the perf bench.
[00:07:43] Marcus Graham: If Dedicated achieves that, what's the expected cost delta?
[00:07:47] Marco Ruiz: We'll provide a modeled cost per million tokens under both Hosted and Dedicated with burst assumptions — that will be in the proposal.
[00:07:55] Samira Patel: For security sign-off we also need a network diagram and change log export.
[00:08:01] Priya Kapoor: We'll include a network diagram for the hosted Dedicated option and the change log export format in the attachments.
[00:08:08] Alex Chen: Wrapping up — recap of decisions and next steps: Redwood to send Dedicated pilot pricing (Alex), run perf benchmark (Marco), share SOC2/BAA and audit log steps (Priya). Solara to provide sample traces and confirm pilot decision timeline (Jenna). Anything else?
[00:08:26] Jenna Lee: No, that covers it. I appreciate the focus.
[00:08:30] Marcus Graham: Thanks all.
[00:08:33] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the deck and action items. Enjoy the holidays.
[00:08:40] Speaker 1: Meeting ended.
